name: Sleep dentistry and snoring appliances
summary: How expats use dental sleep medicine in Singapore for snoring and mild OSA oral appliances — alongside sleep-clinic CPAP pathways, and when a dentist should not be the first stop.
body:
Oral appliance therapy (mandibular advancement devices) can help primary snoring and selected mild-to-moderate obstructive sleep apnoea cases. It sits beside sleep medicine, ENT, and CPAP — not instead of diagnosis.

## Right sequence
- Screen for sleepiness, witnessed apnoeas, hypertension, and morning headaches
- Formal sleep testing when OSA is suspected — do not skip straight to a boil-and-bite mall guard
- Sleep physician or trained dentist collaboration for appliance titration
- Dental assessment of TMJ, periodontal health, and bite before long-term wear

Custom appliances differ sharply from sports mouthguards sold as “anti-snore.”

## CPAP vs appliance
CPAP remains first-line for many moderate–severe OSA diagnoses. Appliances suit CPAP-intolerant patients or travel-heavy expats when clinically appropriate. Combining untreated severe OSA with only a dental device is unsafe.

## How to choose
Look for dentists with sleep-medicine training who require sleep-study documentation and coordinate with respiratory/sleep clinics. Ask about follow-up bite checks, replacement timelines, and what happens if the device worsens jaw pain. Insurance dental riders rarely cover medical OSA devices — check medical benefits language.

## Practical tip
If your partner reports apnoeas or you fall asleep in Grab rides, book sleep assessment first. Bringing a prior home-sleep-test PDF speeds the dental consult when an appliance is already appropriate.
